unit.why: A short anecdote about R. Moshe Leib (of Sasov), who was overcome by the smell of a costly dish while at a nobleman's house to ransom a captive and overcame it by recalling the pleasure of Shabbat Nishmat; it ends with a brief teaching by the narrator's uncle.

stories.start_quote: פ״א היה ההצה״ק ר׳ משה ליב אצל שר
stories.summary_en: While at a nobleman's house to ransom a captive and still fasting that day, R. Moshe Leib was seized by craving at the smell of a very costly dish; he calmed himself by remembering that Nishmat on Shabbat gives far greater delight, and he later told this to his disciple R. Zvi, who taught that each tzaddik has his own 'world' in a different part of the prayers.

tags.why: The Shabbat Nishmat prayer is the means of overcoming the craving, and parts of the liturgy are discussed.

tags.why: The story is transmitted from master to disciple, who adds an interpretation.

quotes: שכל צדיק יש לו עולם בפ״ע
tags.why: A closing teaching by R. Zvi.

quotes: האט ער פיל מער תענוג ממש
tags.why: Spiritual delight in prayer is presented as surpassing bodily pleasure.
Shabbat is the source of the remembered pleasure, though it is not the setting.
The story illustrates the tzaddik's mastery over bodily appetite.
